mainText: This is Dose of Good for Tuesday, November 24. Here are 5 good news stories. First: 16-year-old surfer with low vision becomes world champion. Australian Finn Banks, born with low vision due to albinism, won gold in the vision-impairment division at the World Para Surfing Championship. He scored 19.57 out of 20 in the final and was the youngest member of Australia's team. Second: Tooth-friendly lollipop from a Brazilian university wins innovation prize. The Semeando Sorrisos team from the University of São Paulo's dental school in Bauru took first place in the Sicredi Young Innovators Prize. The lollipop has no added sugar or acidity and contains a protein that may protect against tooth erosion. Its packaging is made from sugarcane bagasse and the stick holds native seeds to plant. Third: Zambian farm turns airline meal leftovers into compost. Loctaguna Organics, near Lusaka, supplies vegetables to an airline caterer and takes back food waste, which becomes compost and pig feed. The farm says this cut its waste-collection costs by 35% and pig-feed costs by 45%. Fourth: Leukaemia can begin 50 years before diagnosis, opening a path to prevention. Using blood samples stored for decades, Cambridge and UCL scientists found that in two-thirds of women who developed acute myeloid leukaemia, the first mutation appeared before age 20. The finding could help detect and prevent the disease, though clinical trials are still needed. Fifth: Wolves help wild blueberries sprout. Blueberry seeds that passed through wolves germinated 96% of the time, against 69% for other seeds, and sprouted faster. The study in northern Minnesota shows wolves also help spread plants through the forest. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
